ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, the vertical axis is “noon solar altitude,” marked with 0°, 30°, 48°, 60°, and 90°; the horizontal axis is date, marked in sequence with E, M, H, N, and F. The curve rises from about 48° on day E, reaches 90° twice before and after day H, and shows a relatively shallow trough near day H; afterward it falls again, reaching about 48° on day F. The question stem also states that M and N are respectively the midpoints of EH and HF, and that on day H the noon sun at this place is located due south. Then reason: the noon solar altitude can reach 90° twice in one year, indicating that this place is located between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn. The two ends E and F are the lower values in the year, about 48°; H is located at the middle trough between the two direct solar irradiations, corresponding to the period when the subsolar point has crossed the local latitude and then reached near a tropic. The question stem gives that on day H the noon sun is due south, indicating that at this time the subsolar point is south of this place. H should correspond to around the Southern Hemisphere summer solstice, that is, the sun is directly overhead near the Tropic of Capricorn, so this place is located in the Southern Hemisphere tropics. From the noon solar altitude of about 48° at E and F, estimated according to the noon solar altitude formula, the latitude of this place is about 18.5°S. The vicinity of 18.5°S is located in the low-latitude trade-wind belt of the Southern Hemisphere, mainly affected by the southeast trade wind.

raw_record.question_text:
The figure below is a schematic diagram of the change in noon solar altitude at a certain place during one year. In the figure, M and N are respectively the midpoints of EH and HF, and on day H the noon sun at this place is located due south. Read the figure and complete the following questions.

<image1>

According to the figure, it can be inferred that the climate of this place is greatly affected by which wind?

method.method_draft: First describe the graph: the place has two dates with noon solar altitude 90°, so it lies inside the tropics; E and F have the annual lower value near 48°, and H is the middle solstitial dip. Use the text clue that on H day the noon Sun is due south to identify H as the Southern Hemisphere summer solstice situation, so the site is in the Southern Hemisphere tropics. From the endpoint altitude near 48° and the solar-altitude formula, estimate the latitude at roughly 18.5°S. A place around 18.5°S lies in the southern trade-wind belt, so its climate is strongly influenced by the southeast trade winds.
method.CoT_raw:
先描述图像：图中纵轴为“正午太阳高度”，标有0°、30°、48°、60°、90°；横轴为日期，依次标出E、M、H、N、F。曲线从E日约48°上升，到H日前后两次达到90°，在H日附近出现一个较浅的低谷；随后又下降，到F日约48°。题干还说明M、N分别为EH、HF的中点，且H日该地正午太阳位于正南方。

再推理：一年中正午太阳高度能两次达到90°，说明该地位于南北回归线之间。E、F两端为一年中的较低值，约48°；H位于两次太阳直射之间的中间低谷，对应太阳直射点越过当地纬度后到达回归线附近的时段。题干给出H日正午太阳在正南方，说明此时太阳直射点在该地以南，H应对应南半球夏至前后，即太阳直射南回归线附近，所以该地位于南半球热带。由E、F处正午太阳高度约48°，按正午太阳高度公式估算，该地纬度约为18.5°S。18.5°S附近位于南半球低纬信风带，主要受东南信风影响。
